# About this document

This is the **project history** of SideQuest (Group 40): everything that has been done to the repository, in order, with the reason behind each step and how to check it. It is meant for three readers:

- a member who was away for a few days and needs to catch up;
- a member preparing the exam, who must be able to explain the whole project and how it was built;
- the authors of the INGSW chapters that describe the process (Git analysis, Sonar report, methodology).

**How it is built.** The document is generated by `npm run history` (`scripts/history.mjs`) from three sources, so it never needs to be written twice:

1. this overview (`docs/history/overview.md`), written by hand: the context needed to understand the log;
2. the **chronological log**: every entry of `PROGRESS.md`, from every member's section, sorted by the commit that recorded it (`git blame`). `PROGRESS.md` is the log every member already updates after each progress step (`CLAUDE.md` §9b), so the quality of this document is the quality of those entries;
3. the **commit history** of the branch and a snapshot of the **task status** (`npm run deps -- --all`).

**How it stays up to date.** The workflow `.github/workflows/history.yml` rebuilds the PDF on every push to `develop` (that is, after every merged PR) and publishes it as the asset of the pre-release `history-latest`, always at the same link: `https://github.com/Mynamesdsuper/sidequest-group40/releases/download/history-latest/SideQuest_Group40_History.pdf`. The generated files are not committed (they are in `.gitignore`), so parallel PRs never conflict on a binary file. Anyone can rebuild it locally with `npm run history` (the PDF lands in `docs/history/`).

**How to read the log.** Each step has the same fields: **What** was done, **Why** (the decision and its alternatives, with links to assumptions A-xx, ADRs or issues), the **Files** touched, **How to verify** it, the **Next / open points**, and the commit or PR. The line under each step title says in which member's section it was written and which commit recorded it.

# The project in brief

**SideQuest** is a web application where users create and play *missions* (ordinary, or secret with a server-side timer), explore them on a map, invite other users, form teams and follow live updates. It is the single product of an **integrated** project for two exams of the Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II, A.A. 2026/27: *Ingegneria del Software* (INGSW) and *Tecnologie Web* (TECWEB). Group 40 chose the **early delivery**: all requirements R01–R12 (core R01–R06, package A R07–R09, package B R10–R12), release by 15 March 2027, submission by 25 March 2027.

| Member | GitHub | Requirements | Also responsible for |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 Vincenzo Pio Lubrano | `vincenzolubrano05` | R01 accounts, R02 missions, R03 exploration, R07 restricted visibility | SRS chapter, Git analysis, README and summary sheet, frontend scaffold (SCAFFOLD-FE) |
| P2 Matteo Marino | `reverinn` | R04 timer, R05 progress and proofs, R06 notifications, R09 capacity and waitlist | UC-01, state diagram, test plan, `TimerPolicy` unit tests, E2E scaffold (SCAFFOLD-E2E) |
| P3 Domenico Panaro | `Mynamesdsuper` | R08 invitations, R10 teams, R11 team participation, R12 live updates | repository admin and coordinator, backend scaffold and CI, architecture chapter, Sonar, traceability, release |

**Technology** (fixed in ADR 0001, justified against the course in ADR 0006): Node.js 22 + TypeScript + Express 5 + Sequelize 6 + PostgreSQL 17 + Socket.IO on the backend; Angular without UI component libraries + Leaflet/OpenStreetMap on the frontend; Jest + supertest and Playwright for tests; Docker, GitHub Actions and SonarCloud for the process. The architecture is a **modular layered monolith**: one folder per module (routes → controller → service/domain → repository/models), modules talk only through their public `index.ts`, *ports* (Strategy + Dependency Injection) and an in-process event bus (Observer).

# How the repository is organised

| Path | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `PROGRESS.md` | the running log of every change, one section per member (source of the chronological log below) |
| `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` | the working rules: ownership, gating, security invariants, commit and PR conventions, Definition of Done |
| `docs/reference/requirements.md` | paraphrase of the official brief, R01–R12 |
| `docs/decisions/` | the 26 domain assumptions A-01..A-26 and the ADRs 0001–0006 |
| `docs/design/` | data model, module contracts (ports, public APIs, events, REST surface), scaffold specification |
| `docs/plan/` | `tasks.json` (every task with owner, dates, blockers), `PLAN.md` and its PDF, `START-HERE.md`, milestones, team |
| `docs/guides/` | one personal guide per member, with the starter prompts for Claude Code |
| `docs/history/` | this document (overview by hand, the rest generated) |
| `scripts/` | Node scripts without dependencies: `validate-plan`, `deps` (gating), `create-issues` (GitHub sync), `directive`, `render-pdf`, `history` |
| `.github/` | `CODEOWNERS`, PR and issue templates, workflows |
| `backend/`, `frontend/`, `e2e/`, `docker/` | not yet created: they come from the scaffold tasks |

# How the team works

- **Branches.** `main` holds releases only; `develop` is the integration branch. All work happens on short branches (`feature/<task>-…`, `docs/…`, `fix/…`, `chore/…`) and enters `develop` through a pull request, squash-merged. Branch protection on `develop` and `main` requires a PR, one approval from a code owner, the `plan` check, and applies to admins too; force pushes are disabled.
- **Ownership.** `CODEOWNERS` gives every path an owner plus a reviewer buddy. Shared code and contracts change only through a *contract-change* issue agreed by all three. Review rotation: P1 ← P2, P2 ← P3, P3 ← P1, within 48 hours.
- **Gating.** A task may start only when all its blockers are DONE (issue closed by a merged PR). `npm run deps -- <TASK>` answers READY or BLOCKED; a workflow keeps the `status:ready` / `status:blocked` labels in sync when issues close.
- **Progress log.** After every step each member adds an entry at the top of their section of `PROGRESS.md`, in the same commit as the work. This is what feeds the chronological log.
- **Directives.** The coordinator can assign instructions as GitHub issues labelled `type:directive` (`npm run directive`); members' sessions list them at start-up.

# Phases so far

*This summary is updated by the coordinator at every milestone; the detailed, always-current record is the chronological log that follows.*

**Phase 0 – Setup (17 Nov 2026, milestone M0, DONE).** The repository was created with documentation and planning only, deliberately without application code, so that the team could agree on requirements, assumptions and contracts before writing code. In order: base configuration and the progress log; the requirements paraphrase, the 26 assumptions and six ADRs; the design drafts (data model, module contracts, realtime events) and the scaffold specification; the working rules (`CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, README, INGSW structure, E2E catalogue); the machine-readable plan with its scripts; the master plan, the three guides and their PDFs; `CODEOWNERS`, templates and the two workflows; finally the GitHub configuration (labels, 9 milestones, one issue per task, the project board, the collaborator invitations) and the branch protection.

**Phase 1 – Hand-over improvements (17 Nov 2026, PR #47, open).** Three additions after the setup: the task CLEANUP before the release candidate, the *Start here* page for the first week, and the coordinator directives.

**Phase 2 – Start of Sprint 0 (from 17 Nov 2026).** P3 prepared the desktop machine (Git, GitHub CLI, Node.js 22, Docker) and cloned the repository. To have all three members productive from the first day, the code scaffold was split into three parallel parts, one per member (SCAFFOLD-BE, SCAFFOLD-FE, SCAFFOLD-E2E), integrated by SCAFFOLD; the issues #51–#53 were created. This history document was added so that every change stays explained and in order.

# Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Task / task ID | a unit of work in `docs/plan/tasks.json` (e.g. `R01`, `SCAFFOLD-FE`), with one GitHub issue labelled `task:<ID>` |
| Blocker | a task that must be DONE before another may start (`blockedBy`) |
| Milestone | a group of tasks with a due date (M0–M8) |
| Code owner | the members `CODEOWNERS` lists for a path; their approval is required to merge changes to it |
| Contract-change | the process to change shared code, contracts or assumptions: issue, agreement of all three, PR reviewed by both others |
| Port | an interface in `backend/src/shared/ports` that one module implements and others use (Strategy + Dependency Injection), with a safe default |
| Squash merge | a PR enters `develop` as a single commit |
